# Default worker native fixture

This is a test-only Base fixture, not a player mod or provider simulation. Canonical metadata targets Factorio 2.1.23; the existing runner must project only engine-family metadata for 2.0.77 and retain the exact source bodies. Its unchanged version 0.1.0 and dependency on MIR put its callbacks after MIR in both source and target. No startup settings are added.

When its own saved key is absent, the first native tick after all mod initializers automatically selects `old-source` for exact published11 or `first` for exact candidate12; other versions refuse. No work is performed by the fixture's on_init. The existing owner must retain the create log and verify that its seed creation did not execute an update. `remote.call("mir-worker-storage-default-native", "begin", mode)` remains available for manual/host use. `first` earns stable native levels4 and5 with a genuine supplied lab, two repeated native-owner queue entries, foreign queued/detached controls and exact science depletion. `old-source` scripts explicitly labelled next levels8/7/6 plus an unpaid4 force, native current/queued/detached partials, then saves with its owned lab stopped. The unchanged fixture observes the candidate upgrade automatically after MIR's configuration callback; optional `upgrade` only verifies that phase. Existing saved/cold state is never initialized again. No provider is present.

Each ordinary completion emits the full after-MIR callback frame before strict structural checks. By that callback end, public4 must be native next5/unresearched with zero saved work, absent from both current research and every queue entry; the first-level debit must be researched and the stable owner must have earned its native level4. Foreign partials and the native bonus must match exactly. All default work, including unpaid level4, moves only during initial migration; ordinary completion changes the public prerequisite and its cancelling debit without moving the native queue. A late-tick prerequisite settlement fails this callback guard. Exact settled current/queue/progress checks follow on the next native tick without inventing a completed-event cursor representation. A real native run must still establish these assertions and closed-save continuity; host checks provide neither acceptance nor permission for a deferred work mirror.

The server owner must observe the named saved marker, actual Saving finished and a closed CRC-clean save, then protect its bytes. Two separate `--benchmark-ticks 1` cold processes read that same immutable save: on_load changes locals only and the first tick emits `cold` after exact frame/lab comparison. No cold grants, lab feed, save, queue/progress write or extra ordinary completion is allowed. The observer never reads or writes MIR storage. Scripted prerequisites, higher levels and foreign partials are setup, not ordinary work.

Modes fail closed on tuple, map price, speed, prototype contract, native bonus/level/flag/work, event order, science and closed-frame drift. Unexpected callbacks emit full observations first. Host controls are only fixture tests; no native pass, synthetic-provider safety, reporter repair, stable acceptance or publication is implied.
